rounds.text: The valuation of Surana Telecom and Power Ltd rests on a fragile foundation of inconsistent profitability that fails to justify long-term confidence. While the current year shows a 15% return on equity [E23], this is a stark outlier compared to the company's historical performance, where the 10-year median return on equity is a meager 4% [E20]. The persistent weakness in capital efficiency is further confirmed by the 5-year median ROE of 5% [E21] and the 3-year median ROE of 7% [E22], which aligns with the official flag of a low 6.67% return on equity over the last three years [E55]. Investors are being asked to pay a premium of 1.33x book value [E2] for a business that offers no dividend yield [E4] and is currently languishing near the bottom of its 52-week range [E5]. Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 7.38 [E1] and maintains a 10-year compounded sales growth of 9% [E8]. Ultimately, the recent uptick in ROE remains unproven against a decade of stagnant returns, suggesting that the current market capitalisation of ₹ 242 Cr [E3] may be overestimating the company's long-term earning power.
